questions.title: In LongRoPE's unified RoPE formula, what exactly is being scaled: positions or frequencies?
questions.question_body: In the paper "LongRoPE: Extending LLM Context Window Beyond 2 Million Tokens", Eq. (1) writes RoPE as \(\cos(n\theta_i), \sin(n\theta_i)\) with \(\theta_i = \theta^{-2i/d}\), and then the unified interpolation (Eq. (2)) looks like \(\cos\big(n/(\lambda (\beta)^i)\big)\) with \(\beta = \theta^{2/d}\). Later, the indicator-based Eq. (3) multiplies the angle by \(\mathbb{I}(\hat{\lambda}_i,\hat{n})\) to get either \(n/\beta^i\) or \(n/(\lambda_i\beta^i)\). I’m confused about the notational consistency: are we scaling the frequencies \(\theta_i\) or the positions \(n\)? Are Eqs. (1)–(3) mathematically equivalent under \(\beta = \theta^{2/d}\), and is \(\lambda\) a per-dimension value (\(\lambda_i\)) or a global one?

questions.title: Why does the paper call \(\lambda=1.0\) "direct extrapolation" in the search space?
questions.question_body: In the search-space description, \(\lambda_i\) ranges from 1.0 to \(1.25\,s\), and 1.0 is described as "direct extrapolation". But with your unified form \(\cos\big(n/(\lambda_i\beta^i)\big)\), \(\lambda_i=1\) looks like "no scaling" (neither interpolation nor extrapolation). Shouldn’t extrapolation correspond to \(\lambda_i<1\) (i.e., increasing effective angle per step)? Is this a terminology issue, or is there a different definition of "extrapolation" being used?

questions.title: Does \(d\) denote per-head dimension in RoPE, and are \(\lambda_i\) shared across heads and layers?
questions.question_body: RoPE is typically applied per attention head. In LLaMA2-7B, \(d_{\text{model}}=4096\), \(n_{\text{heads}}=32\), so \(d_{\text{head}}=128\). In Eq. (1), is \(d\) meant to be \(d_{\text{head}}\) (so there are \(d/2=64\) sine-cosine pairs per head)? When you search per-dimension \(\lambda_i\), are these \(\lambda_i\) values shared across all heads and all layers, or are they distinct per head/layer? Implementation-wise, what exactly is the tensor shape over which \(\lambda_i\) is broadcast?

questions.title: What is the theoretical or empirical justification for the monotonic constraint \(\lambda_i\le \lambda_{i+1}\)?
questions.question_body: The evolution search enforces a non-decreasing \(\lambda_i\) across RoPE dimensions, motivated by NTK intuitions that high-frequency (lower-\(i\)) dimensions should interpolate less. Do you have empirical ablations showing performance with and without this monotonicity? Could the optimal schedule be locally non-monotonic for some models/tasks, and if so, does the constraint prevent reaching better solutions?

questions.title: How is the initial-token threshold \(\hat{n}\) applied with sliding windows and streaming evaluation?
questions.question_body: You keep the first \(\hat{n}\) tokens un-interpolated (\(\lambda_i\) not applied) because early tokens are heavily attended. But for perplexity on long documents you use sliding windows (e.g., size 256 or 256k). Are the "first \(\hat{n}\) tokens" measured relative to the global document start, or relative to each window’s local start? If it is global, how do you handle windows that start well beyond \(\hat{n}\)? If it is local, then each window reintroduces an unscaled prefix, which seems different from the intended global behavior.

questions.title: Does switching the scale at \(n=\hat{n}\) introduce a hard discontinuity, and would a smooth ramp help?
questions.question_body: In Eq. (3), at \(n=\hat{n}\) the factor changes from 1 to \(1/\lambda_i\). This is a hard step. Could this create boundary artifacts in attention around \(\hat{n}\)? Did you try a smooth transition (e.g., a linear or cosine ramp for \(n\in[0,\hat{n}]\)) and compare perplexity or stability?

questions.title: How large is the evolutionary search computationally, and how do you avoid overfitting to a few samples?
questions.question_body: The paper estimates an enormous combinatorial search space (e.g., on the order of \(400^{64}\) for \(d_{\text{head}}=128\) and step 0.01). Practically, how many candidate schedules do you evaluate per target \(L'\)? Roughly how many GPU-hours does a search take for 128k or 256k? Since the fitness is perplexity on only 3–5 long samples (PG19/Books3), how do you reduce overfitting of the found \(\lambda_i,\hat{n}\) to those documents?

questions.title: Exactly how is perplexity computed during search: what context and masking are used?
questions.question_body: When evaluating a candidate schedule, do you compute token-level negative log-likelihood over the entire long document, or only over suffixes (e.g., beyond 4k)? Are you using a fixed sliding-window length, and if so, what attention/memory is available across windows? Clarifying the exact perplexity protocol would help understand what the search is optimizing.

questions.title: How robust are the searched \(\lambda_i\) and \(\hat{n}\) across domains and model families?
questions.question_body: You search on PG19/Books3-like text but evaluate on other datasets and tasks. Do the same schedules transfer well to code/math or dialogue? For Mistral vs LLaMA2, do you need to re-run the full search per model family, or can one family’s schedule initialize the other with minimal loss?

questions.title: How do NTK and YaRN map into your unified notation, and how does LongRoPE differ qualitatively?
questions.question_body: You state that NTK distributes scaling across dimensions (\(\lambda=s^i\) in your text), and YaRN uses three frequency-based groups. In the unified form \(\cos\big(n/(\lambda_i\beta^i)\big)\), could you derive explicitly what \(\lambda_i\) sequences correspond to NTK and YaRN? Qualitatively, are LongRoPE’s learned \(\lambda_i\) closer to a smooth curve (like NTK) or piecewise-constant groups (like YaRN)?

questions.title: How are 2M-token evaluations performed given \(O(n^2)\) attention cost—full context or chunked?
questions.question_body: Naively attending over \(2{,}048\text{k}\) tokens is infeasible for standard dense attention. In the long-sequence experiments you mention sliding windows (e.g., 256k). During Books3 and passkey evaluations, does the model have full attention over the entire \(L'\), or is attention restricted to a window and state is streamed/evicted? If it is chunked/streamed, in what sense is the model truly operating with an effective context of \(\approx 2\text{M}\) tokens?

questions.title: Passkey retrieval at 2M tokens: is the key truly within the active attention window at answer time?
questions.question_body: For the passkey retrieval setup, the key is uniformly placed anywhere up to \(L'=2{,}048\text{k}\). During generation of the answer, does the attention mechanism have access to the entire prefix simultaneously, or do you process the document in chunks and carry some compressed state? If chunked, what guarantees that the key is still represented and not evicted when the question is asked at the end?

questions.title: Why does "position crowding" hurt short-context performance, and how does the 8k readjustment fix it?
questions.question_body: Intuitively, scaling to very large \(L'\) compresses the effective angle changes for small \(n\), making nearby positions harder to distinguish. Could you provide a simple geometric or spectral explanation (e.g., phase increment per token in key dimensions) and show how readjusting to a dedicated 4k/8k schedule restores sufficient angular separation without breaking long-context performance?

questions.title: Clarifying the indicator function in Eq. (3): is it equivalent to dividing by \(\lambda_i\) for \(n\ge\hat{n}\)?
questions.question_body: Eq. (3) defines \(\mathbb{I}(\hat{\lambda}_i,\hat{n})\) so that the angle is \(\cos(\mathbb{I}\cdot n/\beta^i)\), with \(\mathbb{I}=1\) for \(n<\hat{n}\) and \(\mathbb{I}=1/\lambda_i\) for \(n\ge\hat{n}\). This appears to match your earlier \(\cos\big(n/(\lambda_i\beta^i)\big)\) form. Could you confirm this is the intended behavior and that there is no additional \(\beta\) or \(\lambda\) exponent mixing (e.g., the "\(\lambda(\beta)^i\)" notation in Eq. (2))?

questions.title: Why restrict \(\lambda_i\ge 1\)? Did you try allowing \(\lambda_i<1\) (true extrapolation)?
questions.question_body: Your search bounds \(\lambda_i\in[1,1.25s]\). Allowing \(\lambda_i<1\) would enlarge the angle increments and could counteract short-context crowding even for large \(L'\). Did you try \(\lambda_i<1\) and find instability, worse perplexity, or other issues? Is the lower bound mainly a search-efficiency or stability choice?

questions.title: How does the RoPE base \(\theta\) affect LongRoPE, and do schedules transfer across bases?
questions.question_body: In RoPE, \(\theta\) (often \(10^4\)) sets the base frequencies, and \(\beta=\theta^{2/d}\). Some models use larger bases (e.g., \(10^5\) or \(10^6\)). If you learn \(\lambda_i\) for \(\theta=10^4\), can you reuse them for \(\theta=10^6\), or must you re-run the search? Is there a base-invariant way to express the learned schedule (e.g., as a function of normalized frequency)?

questions.title: What are the "catastrophic values" at unseen positions, and can you quantify them?
questions.question_body: The introduction mentions that untrained new position indices introduce catastrophic values and out-of-distribution issues. Do you observe exploding/vanishing attention logits or anomalous layernorm/activation statistics at long positions pre-interpolation? Any histograms or gradients showing how interpolation reduces these pathologies?

questions.title: Why two-stage fine-tuning (128k then 256k) instead of one-stage 256k, and how sensitive is it?
questions.question_body: For LLaMA2 you fine-tune 400 steps at 128k and then 600 at 256k, rather than training 1000 steps directly at 256k. Do you have ablations showing this two-stage approach converges better or reaches better minima? How sensitive are the results to the split, learning rate schedule, and the choice of starting from the 128k-optimized \(\lambda_i\)?

questions.title: How should one switch between 8k-tuned and 2048k-tuned schedules during inference without artifacts?
questions.question_body: You propose readjusting RoPE for short contexts and say that during inference, if the sequence length is less than 8k, you update RoPE with the short-length rescale factors. If a generation starts short and later exceeds 8k, should we switch \(\lambda_i\) mid-stream? Would that cause inconsistencies in QK dot products for already cached keys/values? What is the recommended implementation for streaming servers?

questions.title: Are there theoretical limits from RoPE periodicity that constrain usable \(L'\) (phase aliasing)?
questions.question_body: Since RoPE uses \(\cos(n\theta_i)\), each dimension has period \(T_i=2\pi/\theta_i\). As \(n\) grows to millions, low-frequency dimensions will wrap many times. Do you risk position collisions or aliasing that degrade uniqueness at \(L'=2{,}048\text{k}\)? How does LongRoPE’s non-uniform scaling affect these periods, and are there principled limits on the maximum safe context length?
